In plain language; reframing: the output methods is for your own code structures, above all a transaction or a timeout that your code controls (`methods` 1 to 2: the sentence of the reframing names it).  Numerals 1 to 4 are new: the steps of the method as a numbered list, in the old order

In plain language.  The section opens with the default case, GetUser in UserRepositoryExtensions (`GetUser` 0 to 1, `internal` 4 to 5, `DbConnection` 2 to 3).  `methods` 1 to 0: "A `methods` method" became "A method that takes a connection"

In plain language, one rule to a bullet (`public` 4 to 6: the bullet on the visibility of the class names it in each sentence).  Old: "The extension class is in the type's namespace, not nested ..., and is named after the type's own name alone".  New: two bullets, "It is not nested in the types around the type" and "named after the name of the type alone".  Same rules.  Old: "When it is not, or when a type of your project or a model has the class's full name, the type gets none of its methods there: SQLSRC276."  New: "A type gets none of its methods in an extension class that cannot be written", when two types that share it give it two visibilities, or a type of your project or a model has its full name; and "only when the class is public for both or internal for both".  Same rule.  Old: "A method there is not named like a member of DbConnection or object ..., nor like the class itself (SQLSRC274)."  New: two bullets, "cannot have the name of a member of DbConnection or object" and "cannot have the name of the class itself", each with SQLSRC274 (SQLSRC274 4 to 5).  Same rules

In plain language.  Old: "A method is then not named like a member of the type, ... nor like a nested class of the type's queries (SQLSRC274)."  New: "The method cannot have the name of one of these (SQLSRC274)", the three as a list.  Same rule.  Old: "A method is then not named like a constant or token method ... (SQLSRC274), nor like the class (SQLSRC009)."  New: "cannot have the name of one of these", a list with SQLSRC274 and SQLSRC009 each on its own item.  Same rule.  Old: "Two methods of one name in one class, ... are SQLSRC274, and so are two methods of one name and one list of arguments in two extension classes of one namespace, which a call could not tell apart."  New: "Two methods are SQLSRC274 in one of these cases", the two cases as a list; "A call could not tell them apart" stays.  Same rule
In plain language: the three cases of the Async suffix, one sentence each; the name without the suffix shown as `ListFrom`, the sample's (`ListFrom` 0 to 1)

In plain language, one rule to a bullet.  CA2100 (numeral 2100 1 to 2): the list parameter's bullet names it, where the old "Nor does" pointed at it.  Old: "... that text is your own code's choice, never a user's, as tokens says."  New: "That text is the choice of your own code, never of a user".  Same rule.  Old: "The names of the arguments a query method can have, ..., are not names a token can have (SQLSRC275)."  New: "A token cannot have the name of an argument that a query method can have (SQLSRC275)", then the five names.  Same rule.  The link to parameters.md#list-limit is on each of the two bullets that the old sentence became

In plain language, one rule to a bullet.  Opens "when its State is Closed, and closes it again" and "a connection that was not closed is left as it was" are two bullets side by side.  The bold lead-in Give the method the transaction stays whole, quoted by tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer.SyncAsync/KnownDifferences.cs.  Old: "On SQL Server, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient refuses a command on a connection that has a transaction the command was not given, and throws InvalidOperationException (...) before anything is sent."  New: "If a command was not given the transaction of its connection, each driver does a different thing", then a bullet for each driver, the message letter for letter.  Same rule, checked against KnownDifferences.cs

In plain language.  The term first: UnexpectedRowCountException says that a query returned the wrong number of rows.  The two shapes are a list of cases joined by "one of these": `one` with no rows or more than one, `one-optional` with more than one.  The message, QueryName, the collection method's message and ItemIndex are one rule to a bullet, each message letter for letter.  Old: "a query method's `ItemIndex` is null".  New: "If a query method throws it, its `ItemIndex` is null."  Same rule
In plain language: "so code that catches that" names `InvalidOperationException` (`InvalidOperationException` 2 to 3)

Text of feature work, in plain language: two bullets, the namespace and the visibility.  Old: "It is in the namespace `SqlSource`, generated into every project that uses SqlSource, unless the project uses the copy of the one project it references that has it".  New: "SqlSource generates it into every project that uses SqlSource.  A project gets no copy of its own when it uses the copy of the one project it references that has it."  Same rule.  The "unless" of the visibility stays in its lead-in, and "only when it sees it" stays

In plain language.  The term first, then "It is SQL Server's alone".  The four conditions are a list joined by "all of these": takes a connection at `one`, `one-optional` or `many`; given a transaction; threw an exception of its own or reached a database error for a row or a statement after the rows; a later error of the query rolled the transaction back.  The four kinds of InnerException are a list joined by "one of these".  The later error, the message letter for letter, QueryName, the first exception thrown as it is, the error that itself rolled back, the completed transaction refused, and the wrapping library are one rule to a bullet (`TransactionRolledBackException` 2 to 3, `InvalidOperationException` 3 to 4: "this exception" names its type).  Old: "A transaction of a library that wraps Microsoft.Data.SqlClient's and keeps its `Connection` set after it completes is neither refused nor reported".  New: "A library can wrap the transaction of Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.  If the wrapper keeps its `Connection` set after it completes, the method neither refuses nor reports it."  Same rule.  Checked against src/SqlSource/Generation/Exceptions/ExceptionSource.cs (QueryName, the message, InnerException) and ExecutionCapabilityRules.cs and ExecutionCapabilityWriter.cs (SQL Server alone, the methods that read rows, the check of the transaction's Connection)

By the brief: the bullet "On PostgreSQL, no method throws it", what PostgreSQL does instead: an error aborts the transaction, the method throws it as Npgsql's `PostgresException` (`PostgresException` 0 to 1), and PostgreSQL refuses each later command in the transaction until you roll it back; links databases/postgresql/query-methods.md#method-results.  Sources: ExecutionCapabilityRules.cs (a PostgreSQL method has none of the flags that throw TransactionRolledBackException), tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres/EndToEnd/StreamingQueryTests.cs (StreamNumbersFailingHalfway_BreakInATransaction_AbortsTheTransaction: 25P02) and MethodQueryTests.cs (the database's error thrown as PostgresException)
In plain language: the collection method's InnerException is its own sentence, and "so code that catches that" names `InvalidOperationException`

Text of feature work, in plain language.  Old: "..., beside which it is generated, so another assembly catches it by type only when it sees it, and as `InvalidOperationException` otherwise".  New: "beside which SqlSource generates it.  So another assembly catches it by its type only when it sees it.  Otherwise, that assembly catches it as `InvalidOperationException`".  Same rule; "only" stays

In plain language.  The term first: CollectionItemException says that the database reported an error at one item of a collection method.  InnerException, ItemIndex with QueryName, the message letter for letter, and "catch it where your code would catch the exception of the driver" are one rule to a bullet; "as above" became "as the sample does"

In plain language, one rule to a bullet: the base type, the members passed on, and the target of another project.  Old: "that project targets .NET 6 or later ...: one built for netstandard2.0 or netstandard2.1 alone cannot pass on the first three, and your project gets SQLSRC038".  New: "that project must target .NET 6 or later", with SQLSRC038 two sentences on; "alone" stays.  Old: "An exception of the method's own ... and an error that no item raised, are thrown as ... says".  New: the two in two sentences, "So is an error that no item raised".  Same rule; "only" stays in the lead-in

Text of feature work, in plain language.  Old: "..., beside which it is generated, so another assembly catches it by type only when it sees it, and as `DbException` otherwise".  New: "beside which SqlSource generates it.  So another assembly catches it by its type only when it sees it.  Otherwise, that assembly catches it as `DbException`".  Same rule; "only" stays

In plain language, in the order of a setting's section: what it does, the values (`true`, ignoring case, makes them public; any other value leaves them internal), the default (without the property they are internal), the place, the precedence, the error (`public` 1 to 2, `true` 1 to 2: the bullet of the values names both).  Old: "any other value, and none, leaves them `internal`".  New: "Any other value leaves them `internal`" and "Without the property, they are `internal`".  Same rule.  Checked against src/SqlSource/Generation/Exceptions/PublicExceptions.cs

In plain language, one rule to a bullet.  "It is a property of the project file, and not a setting of a settings file" stays word for word.  Old: "Public exceptions are part of its public API, and an app that references two such libraries sees two copies: it gets SQLSRC022 if it uses SqlSource, and an error that the name is ambiguous where it names one if it does not."  New: the API sentence, then the bullet "An app that references two such libraries sees two copies", with the two cases each condition first.  Same rule

In plain language, one rule to a bullet.  The attributes, and the three conversion classes, are two bullets; the three kinds of types the classes read and send are a list, each link kept.  The extern alias, the test project, the visibility, "whatever it sets", SQLSRC022 with the shared project, SQLSRC023 and SQLSRC038 are each a bullet.  Old: "the others' internals", "the other's internals".  New: "the internals of the others", "the internals of the other".  Same rules; "only", "unless", "alone" and "whatever" stay.  Checked against tests/SqlSource.Tests/Generator/ExceptionReuseTests.cs (Build_FriendOnlyUnderAnAlias_WritesItsOwn, Build_FriendReachedFromGlobal_IsUsed)

In plain language, five sentences.  Old: "Each project sees only its own copies, and a project that sees the other's internals and does not use SqlSource does not see them at all."  New: "Each project sees only its own copies.  A project that sees the internals of the other and does not use SqlSource does not see them at all."  Same rule.  "(CS0436)" became "warning CS0436"

The limit in its three parts.  What you see: the three exceptions cannot be caught by type, or two copies give SQLSRC022 or the compiler's error that the name is ambiguous.  Why: "caught by their type only where they are seen", and a project sees them by InternalsVisibleTo or SqlSourcePublicExceptions.  What to do: one shared project for two copies (SQLSRC022 2 to 3: the fix names it again), else catch InvalidOperationException and DbException.  Old: "UnexpectedRowCountException, TransactionRolledBackException and CollectionItemException are caught by their type only where they are seen.  A project that sees another's exceptions, because the other grants it InternalsVisibleTo or sets SqlSourcePublicExceptions, catches them by type."  New: "These exceptions are caught by their type only where they are seen.  A project sees the exceptions of another project when the other grants it InternalsVisibleTo, or sets SqlSourcePublicExceptions."  Same rule; "only" stays

The limit in its three parts.  The sentence of 92 words is a list of its four conditions, joined by "all of these", then CS0419 for the exception itself and CS1574 for a member, each a bullet with its example.  Why: at a cref the compiler finds the copy that the project cannot see too, so the name has two copies.  What to do: the documentation ID, T:, P: and M: each a bullet (`cref` 3 to 6: "the `cref`" is named in the conditions).  Checked against tests/SqlSource.Tests/Generator/ExceptionReuseTests.cs: Build_UserCrefWithAStrangersCopyReferenced_IsAWarning (CS0419, CS1574) and Build_UserCrefAsADocumentationIdWithAStrangersCopyReferenced_HasNoDiagnostic

Only then does it read the next 1,000."  Same rule; "only" stays.  "So a bad item is found only after" became "The method finds a bad item only after"; "there" became "in those two cases"

In plain language, two bullets: all or nothing, with the four kinds of throw in one sentence; the transaction the database has already rolled back.  Checked against BatchWriter.cs (rollback when anything throws, skipped when the transaction's Connection is null, the first exception thrown)

In plain language, three bullets: used as it is, "whatever" stays; what ran is still in it, yours to decide; on SQL Server a completed transaction is refused.  "A `methods` method given a `transaction`" became "At the output `methods`, a collection method that is given a `transaction`"

In plain language, three bullets: "So is an ambient transaction" became "An ambient transaction is used as it is too"; a connection not in it; the way for a repository, which now links repositories.md#repository-transactions, an anchor that exists.  Old: "A connection that is not in it, such as one opened before the scope and never enlisted, or one whose connection string turns enlisting off, runs the items in no transaction at all, as under `transaction=off`."  New: "A connection that is not in the ambient transaction runs the items in no transaction at all, as under `transaction=off`.  Examples are a connection opened before the scope and never enlisted, and one whose connection string turns enlisting off."  Same rule; "not" stays.  "Whatever" stays

By the brief, which asks the section to say what happens on PostgreSQL and on SQL Server: the bullet "Under `off`, what a failed item leaves in the database depends on the database" (PostgreSQL rolls back the round trip of the failed item, the round trips before it stay; SQL Server commits each item on its own; on both the round trips after it do not run), and the bullet "On PostgreSQL, a database error aborts the caller's transaction", consistent with exceptions.md#transaction-rolled-back.  Each restates its database's page, databases/postgresql/query-methods.md#collection-methods and databases/sqlserver/query-methods.md#collection-methods, and links it.  Checked against tests/DatabaseTests/Postgres/EndToEnd/BatchQueryTests.cs (InsertNoteNoTransaction_NullItemInTheSecondChunk_KeepsTheFirstChunk, InsertNote_DuplicateKeyInTheCallersTransaction_LeavesItsRollbackToTheCaller) and tests/DatabaseTests/SqlServer/EndToEnd/BatchQueryTests.cs (InsertNote_DuplicateKeyInTheCallersTransaction_LeavesTheOtherItemsInIt)

Text of feature work.  The limit in its three parts, with its own symptom, `NotSupportedException` from a collection method, apart from the `InvalidCastException` of query-methods.md#limit-wrapped-connection.  What you see: the three failures, a list joined by "one of these", the message "Specified method is not supported." letter for letter.  Why: "A collection method works fully only on the connection of the driver itself", then the kind of wrapper behind each failure (`NotSupportedException` 2 to 3, `InvalidCastException` 1 to 2: the Why names each).  What to do: the driver's connection that the wrapper holds, the link to the query method's limit kept.  Old: "A collection method works fully only on the driver's own connection.  On a `DbConnection` that wraps the driver's, it can fail where the query method works, in three ways."  New: "On a `DbConnection` that wraps the connection of the driver, a collection method can fail where the query method works.  You see one of these:" and "A collection method works fully only on the connection of the driver itself."  Same rule; "only" stays.  Old: "And a wrapper whose batches hold commands of its own runs the items, but a database error at an item is thrown as the driver's own exception, ..., not as `CollectionItemException`, so nothing names the item."  New: "The items run, but a database error at an item is thrown as the exception of the driver, ....  It is not thrown as `CollectionItemException`, so nothing names the item."  Same rule; "not" stays.  Not checked against a test: no test runs a collection method on a wrapper; the words are kept
